chunks: With this chain of transmission, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from ʿUthmān ibn ʿĪsā, from Samāʿah, who said:

A woman in istiḥāḍah, if the blood penetrates the cotton, performs ghusl for every two prayers, and for al-fajr one ghusl. But if the blood does not pass beyond the cotton, then she must perform ghusl once each day and wudu (ablution) for every salat (prayer). And if her husband wishes to approach her, then it is when she performs ghusl. This is when it is fresh blood; but if it is yellowish discharge, then she must perform wudu (ablution).

key_terms.اغْتَسَلَتْ: she performed ghusl, a ritual bath
key_terms.الْكُرْسُفَ: cotton used to check or absorb bleeding
key_terms.الْمُسْتَحَاضَةُ: a woman experiencing istiḥāḍah, irregular non-menstrual bleeding
key_terms.غُسْلًا: ritual bath required in the ruling

ai.seo_question: What are the rulings of ghusl and wudu (ablution) for a woman in istiḥāḍah according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives legal rulings for a woman experiencing istiḥāḍah, distinguishing between heavier and lighter bleeding by whether the blood penetrates the cotton. It also clarifies the required ghusl and wudu (ablution) for salat (prayer), and mentions the ruling related to marital relations in this state.
